provider: nightly.link (GitHub Actions artifact -> anonymous URL wrapper)

free_tier.stated: No quota of its own — it is a public-read proxy over GitHub Actions artifacts, which are themselves uncounted for public repos but capped at 90-day retention. Service is 'provided totally free of charge'.

retention.stated: No quota of its own — it is a public-read proxy over GitHub Actions artifacts, which are themselves uncounted for public repos but capped at 90-day retention

egress.terms: Free. Redirects to productionresultssa*.blob.core.windows.net (Azure Blob, GitHub's artifact store) with a signed URL, so downloads never touch GitHub's HTML front end.

tooling: oprypin/nightly.link, 1011 stars, AGPL, self-hostable (Go). URL grammar is deterministic: https://nightly.link/<owner>/<repo>/workflows/<workflow>/<branch>/<artifact>.zip
chaining: This is the multiplier that makes GitHub Actions artifacts usable at all: it converts 'artifact behind a login' into 'plain CDN URL'. Combined with unlimited public repos and the 90-day max retention it becomes a rolling 90-day hot tier of unlimited size, refreshed by scheduled workflows.
limits_note: Inherits GitHub artifact TTL (max 90 days for public repos) and the artifact size cap. Anonymous users share one global GitHub API rate limit — the site explicitly warns 'The throttling will likely become very bad over time' unless you install their GitHub App on your repo.
reliability_note: Single-maintainer free service — a single point of failure if you depend on the hosted instance. Self-host it for production use. Rate limiting is the real bite, not storage.

evidence.proved: 'Any public repository is accessible by default and visitors don't need to log in'; 'don't share the global API rate limit ... throttling will likely become very bad over time'
